title: Part 5 analysis.json: the fields a report across a person's takes should read
purpose: A versioned allowlist of the analysis.json fields Part 7's pattern finder and Ask read when they compare takes over time. Each entry says what the field means, its units, which way is worse (and, for a letter grade, the order of its letters), which side convention it uses, the schema version it first appears in, whether it is stable or additive, when it is written and what changed across versions. The machine-readable types and enums stay in contracts/analysis.schema.json; this file adds the meaning the schema does not carry. tests/test_contract_history_fields.py pins every path against the schema and every since against the committed examples.

entry_keys.path: The field, written as in contracts/analysis.schema.json: a dot between objects, [] for one item of an array.
entry_keys.units: degrees, metres, seconds, score points, ratio (follower seconds per example second), fraction (0 to 1), count, index, millimetres (quality.signals.position_jitter_mm, per frame), or none for a label, a code, a list or a fingerprint.
entry_keys.direction: Which way is worse. One of the keys of direction_values.
entry_keys.order: Only on an entry whose value is a letter grade or a list of them (score.grade; score.credit.grade and score.credit.grades): its letters, best first, the same list as the schema's enum for the field. Rank letters by it, never by the alphabet: A, B, C, D, F for score.grade and S, A, B, C, D, E, F for the credit.
entry_keys.side_convention: subject_own where the field names a left or a right, otherwise null. See side_convention.
entry_keys.since: The analysis schema version the path first appears in. A path whose set of values grew keeps its first version here and the version of each later value in notes.
entry_keys.stability: One of the keys of stability_values.
entry_keys.presence: One of the keys of presence_values.
entry_keys.present_when: Only on an entry whose presence is conditional: the condition, in words.
entry_keys.notes: What changed across versions, and what to do or not do with the field.

direction_values.none: The field is a label, a time, a count, a code or a fingerprint. It does not rank one take above another.
direction_values.larger_absolute_is_worse: The further the number is from zero, in either sign, the further the follower is from the example. The sign says which side of the example, not better or worse.
direction_values.lower_is_worse: A bigger number is better, so a smaller one is worse.
direction_values.later_letter_is_worse: The grades run in their own order, best first, and a later letter in that order is worse: A, B, C, D, F for score.grade (A is best); S, A, B, C, D, E, F for score.credit.grade (S is best, see score.credit.grades). The entry's order key lists its letters in that order: rank by it, never by the alphabet, in which S would come last.
direction_values.away_from_one_is_worse: 1.0 is the example's pace. The further the ratio is from 1.0, the bigger the pace difference. Under the rehab profile a ratio above 1.15 is not held against the take.
direction_values.present_is_worse: The entry exists because something was found or capped. An empty or missing list is the better case.

stability_values.stable: The name, type, units and meaning have not changed since the version in since.
stability_values.additive: A later minor version widened it (a new value, a new code, a meaning that grew), or its words are template text that may be revised. Read it as open: tolerate a value you do not know. The notes say what changed.

presence_values.always: In every document written at or after since. A document older than that is the only case where it is missing.
presence_values.per_fault: On every entry of faults[] of a document written at or after since.
presence_values.when_compared: In every document at or after since whose take was aligned and compared. Absent from the zero score of a take that could not be aligned.

side_convention.subject_own: left and right are the performer's own left and right, as the skeleton files name them (left_* joints, x positive toward the subject's left). They are never the image's left or the viewer's, and they do not depend on the camera angle. Part 5 applies no mirroring of its own to a clip, because Part 3 gives the body in the subject's own frame; only a feet side file marked mirrored has its left and right series swapped. Mirror a field yourself only when you draw a mirrored view.
side_convention.both: The same measure in the same direction on the left and the right, merged into one fault when their frames overlap. Its size is the mean of the two sides, and its joint has the side taken off (shoulder, not left_shoulder). A profile can keep a fault on one side that fitness reports on both. When matching faults across takes, treat both as covering left and right.
side_convention.center: A measure with no side: trunk_lean_forward, trunk_lean_side, shoulder_tilt and head_forward. Its joint is spine, shoulders or neck.
side_convention.sources: contracts/analysis.schema.json (faults[].side: the subject's own sides), CONTRACT.md (common to every accepted file: x the subject's left), part5/measures.py, part5/words.py, part5/lateral.py.

compare_like_with_like: Compare a score only with a score that has the same score.version and the same profile. Equal score.params_sha256 means identical scoring parameters; a different one under the same score.version means the parameters were retuned, so treat it as another scale. Compare fault sizes by dividing magnitude_deg by threshold_deg, within one profile, because each measure has its own threshold. Group faults by measure, side and direction, never by text or cue. Leave out of fault counts any document with a refusal status or with warnings, or count them apart.

absent_means.fault: A measure, side and direction that is not in faults[] was either (1) compared and stayed within its threshold or did not last long enough to count, (2) compared, came past a threshold, and was dropped: it is then listed in diagnostics.near_misses, or (3) not compared at all. It is not compared when the camera did not see it (the sided measure is in diagnostics.visibility.excluded), when it is a foot measure and the foot measure is not in diagnostics.feet.compared (without a feet file there is no diagnostics.feet and no foot fault can exist), when the follower declared it not scored (1.14.0: the sided measure is in body_mask.not_scored_measures), or when the take could not be aligned (no detection ran, so faults is empty and diagnostics.near_misses is absent). Under the dance and rehab profiles the thresholds are looser, so an absent fault there does not mean absent under fitness. With a low_match warning the measures were compared on a poor match, so an absent fault is weak evidence.
absent_means.tempo: A tempo whose ratio is null was not measured. It is never on time. It is null for every tempo of a take with match.quality low, score.per_rep[].tempo_ratio included (TICKET-063, ADR-0014 Amendment 4: the alignment covers only part of the take, so the time it spans says nothing about how fast the take was done) and for a stretch where the example side spans under 1 s. On time is a ratio from 0.85 to 1.15 with a null cue. A document written before TICKET-063 (2026-11-01) can still carry a number for a low match take, under the same schema_version, so treat tempo as not measured whenever match.quality is low. An absent score.tempo means the document is older than 1.5.0 or its take could not be aligned; an absent window tempo also means the window was not compared.
absent_means.measure: The document has no list of the measures it compared. diagnostics.visibility says how many were usable and which were left out, and only when some were left out. A measure that appears in no field of the document is therefore neither flagged nor proven fine: it is fine only when status.code is ok (a refusal from before 1.4.0 has faults [] and no warnings, and nothing was compared), the take has no warnings, the measure is not in diagnostics.visibility.excluded and, for a foot measure, it is in diagnostics.feet.compared. Otherwise it was not measured.
absent_means.near_misses: diagnostics.near_misses lists the candidates detection considered and dropped (a measure, side and direction with at least one frame past its threshold that was not reported). It is not a list of faults and never changes the score. total 0 with items [] means nothing came past a threshold. The field absent means the take could not be aligned or the document is older than 1.8.0. items holds at most 10, largest first, and omitted counts the rest.
absent_means.score_fields: score.fault_cap absent: the take reports no fault, or its score.version is simon.score.v1. score.uncapped absent: no cap lowered the value. score.capped_by absent: no warning; present: the take had warnings, whether or not the cap lowered the value (it never names the fault cap). score.per_rep absent: the take was compared as a whole. faults[].reps and faults[].rep_sizes absent for the same reason.
absent_means.warnings_and_match: warnings and match are written only for a take that earned a warning. Both absent means no warning and a good enough match; Part 7's own no_person document has no match because nothing was compared.

score_versions.read: Read score.version. It names the score a document was made with and is not the same as schema_version: ADR-0018's fallback shipped simon.score.v1 inside analysis 1.10.0, and after make score-fallback a 1.11.0 document carries v1 again.
score_versions.the_score_only: v1, v2 and v3 differ in how a fault and a take are charged and capped, which means score.value, score.grade, score.fault_cap and score.uncapped. Measure names, sides, directions and sizes are detection. ADR-0018 states that detection reads none of the v2 changes and is byte identical, and ADR-0019 keeps detection byte identical, so a measure name and its magnitude_deg in a v1 take mean what they mean in a v3 take. Nothing is renamed or rescaled by a score version.
score_versions.unchanged_in_all_three: The penalty curve (base, slope, cap), the similarity term, the grade bands (A 90 and above, B 80 to 89, C 70 to 79, D 60 to 69, F below 60), the take being the mean of its windows (ADR-0013), and the cap of 59 (grade F) for a take with a warning (ADR-0012).

simon.score.v1.analysis_schema: from 1.2.0. The only score of every document up to 1.9.0.
simon.score.v1.rule: Each fault costs min(cap, base + slope * (r minus 1)), where r is |magnitude_deg| / threshold_deg, weighted by how much of the clip it covers and by its coverage. A similarity term takes off up to s_max points. value is 100 minus both, rounded half up.
simon.score.v1.uncapped: From 1.9.0: the value before the warning cap, written only when that cap lowered the value.
simon.score.v1.status: Shipped. ADR-0018 and ADR-0019 both fall back to it with make score-fallback.

simon.score.v2.rule: v1's formula with each miss also weighted by how much the trainer moves that measure in its window, never below range_floor, so a miss on a measure the exercise does not move costs less. A take that reports any fault is capped at 89 (score.fault_cap 89).
simon.score.v2.uncapped: The value before every cap: the fault cap and the warning cap. With both, the value before the first.
simon.score.v2.status: Not shipped. It failed held-out score seed 59 (target 5), so v1 was put back; the v2 code stays in the tree. The schema allows it, so read score.version. Whether any stored document carries it is not determinable from this repository.

simon.score.v3.rule: v2's weight and its cap of 89 for one reported fault, and a second cap of 79 (the top of C) for a take whose faults list holds two or more entries. The cap is applied once, to the mean of the windows; a window and per_rep keep their own values.
simon.score.v3.fault_cap: 89 for one reported fault, 79 for two or more. Read it, never assume 89.
simon.score.v3.status: Shipped by the rules in this tree. It held all five targets on held-out score seed 61 (docs/thresholds-score-v3.md).

score_changes_without_a_version.what: ADR-0013 (05312b7): the score.value of a simon.score.v1 take became the mean of its windows (one window per repetition, or about 5 s slices of a take compared as a whole), and score.basis and score.timeline were added. A take of one window (under 7.5 s, or one repetition) scores exactly as before. A longer take can score lower: the ADR's real lateral raise take of 8 repetitions went from no faults and 90 or more to 77, a C.
score_changes_without_a_version.marked_by: Nothing at the time. score.version stayed simon.score.v1, score.params_sha256 did not change (part5/rules.json was not touched) and schema_version was not changed: it stayed 1.2.0, 1.3.0 or 1.4.0 by the content of the document, as before (part5/output.py wrote 1.4.0 for a take with a warning, else 1.3.0 for a take compared by repetition, else 1.2.0). score.basis and score.timeline were written in all three from that commit until d3250dc made the schema 1.5.0, so a 1.2.0, 1.3.0 or 1.4.0 document (by content) can hold them. A v1 score.value from before this change is not on the same scale as one after it for a take longer than one window.

detection_changes_without_a_version.what: Attempt 4 (ADR-0017, TICKET-044): trunk_lean_side is now measured so that it stays between -90 and 90 degrees through a deep forward hinge; before, it wrapped (155 degrees on a real Romanian deadlift). Its sign is unchanged (positive toward the subject's left). Persistence is judged per example repetition, and an example of two or more repetitions is always compared repetition by repetition, so its faults carry reps and score.basis is reps.
detection_changes_without_a_version.marked_by: Nothing. schema_version stayed 1.8.0 (1.9.0 came later the same day), so a 1.8.0 document can come from either side of the change and every document from 1.9.0 on has it. score.version does not change. A trunk_lean_side size from before this date is not comparable when the trunk hinged forward past about 90 degrees.

detection_changes_without_a_version.what: Attempt 5 (ADR-0015 Amendment 4, ADR-0017): a foot measure that jitters is not read (the far foot of a side view), so a foot measure the earlier rules compared can now be left out.
detection_changes_without_a_version.marked_by: diagnostics.feet.usable and compared, only on a document that has a feet file.

detection_changes_without_a_version.what: TICKET-063 (ADR-0014 Amendment 4): every tempo of a take with match.quality low is null.

measures.units: degrees for every measure. magnitude_deg is follower minus example, signed. direction more is a positive difference and less a negative one. A measure is a joint angle (measure_kind angle) or the direction of a segment (measure_kind direction). The only length in a fault is lateral_m, in metres.
measures.worse: For every measure, more and less are both departures from the example, and a bigger |magnitude_deg| is worse. Neither direction is better.
measures.side: left, right or both for a per-side measure; center for the four torso and head measures.

elbow_flexion.more: the elbow bent more than the example (0 is a straight arm, and the angle grows as it bends)

knee_flexion.more: the knee bent more (0 is a straight leg)

upper_arm_out.more: the upper arm further out from the body, in the frontal plane
upper_arm_out.less: the upper arm closer to the body

upper_arm_forward.more: the upper arm raised further forward, measured against the trunk (0 is hanging along the trunk)
upper_arm_forward.less: the arm not raised far enough forward (the timed words say too low)

forearm_out.more: the forearm, and so the hand, further out from the body

thigh_out.more: the thigh, and so the knee, further out from the body

thigh_forward.more: the thigh raised higher (0 is straight down)

foot_out.more: the foot further out from under the hip (feet further apart)

knee_valgus.more: the knee caving in: the knee's offset inside the hip to ankle line over the thigh length, in degrees

trunk_lean_forward.more: leaning forward more than the example

trunk_lean_side.more: leaning further toward the subject's left than the example
trunk_lean_side.less: leaning further toward the subject's right

shoulder_tilt.more: the left shoulder higher than in the example

head_forward.more: the head further forward of the shoulders, with the trunk's lean taken off

foot_rotation.more: the foot turned out (toes pointing away from the midline, against the pelvis's forward) more than the example
foot_rotation.less: the foot not turned out enough

ankle_inversion.more: the foot on its outer edge, the ankle rolling out
ankle_inversion.less: the foot on its inner edge, the ankle rolling in

fields.meaning: The analysis schema version the document was written under.
fields.notes: A document without it is schema 1.0. It says which fields to expect, not which score or detection build made the document: read score.version for the score. Since 1.5.0 every new document carries the current version; before that a document kept the version of the latest group it used (1.2.0, 1.3.0, 1.4.0).

fields.meaning: The analysis profile that produced the document: dance, rehab or fitness today.
fields.notes: A document without it (before 1.7.0) is fitness. The names are data in part5/profiles.json, so a new profile can appear. A score and a fault set are read within one profile: dance and rehab loosen the position tolerances, so for the same take they never report a fault fitness does not, and their grades are not comparable with fitness (ADR-0016).

fields.meaning: The limb chains the follower declared not scored: seated, or not using an arm, a forearm or a leg (ADR-0023).
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask (part5 analyse --mask, or the mask field of POST api/analyse).
fields.notes: Absent means the whole body was scored. A score and a fault set are read within one mask, as within one profile: the score is taken on the remaining measures, so never rank or average a masked take with an unmasked one or with another mask. An absent fault on a measure in not_scored_measures says nothing about that limb.

fields.meaning: The presets and chains as declared, each once, in the order given.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: Presets: seated (both legs) and full_body (nothing masked, alone). Chains: left_arm, right_arm (from the shoulder), left_forearm, right_forearm (from the elbow), left_leg, right_leg (from the hip). Group takes by the chains the mask expands to, not by these words: seated and left_leg, right_leg are the same mask.

fields.meaning: Where the mask came from: cli or api.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: It changes nothing in the analysis.

fields.meaning: The chains with at least one measure scored.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: With not_scored_chains it lists each of the six chains once. An arm whose forearm alone is masked is listed here, its upper arm still scored.

fields.meaning: The chains whose every measure was dropped from detection and the score.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: A masked arm lists its forearm too. Compare a chain across takes only where it is scored in each.

fields.meaning: The canonical joints masked, the ones below the joint each chain hangs from.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: The joints of faults[].joints. A leg also masks the heel and toes of a feet file, which are not canonical joints and are not listed.

fields.meaning: The sided body and foot measures dropped (left_elbow_flexion, right_foot_rotation and so on).
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: No fault, miss, insight or near miss of the document names one; part5.output.validate_analysis refuses a document where one does. Leave these measures out of a pattern across takes for this take.

fields.meaning: The plain words to show beside the score, such as Legs not scored, by your setting.
fields.present_when: The follower declared a mask.
fields.notes: Template text that may be revised; read the chain lists, never this text, to tell masks apart.

fields.meaning: How the analysis ended: a code and a sentence.
fields.notes: A document with no status is a 1.0 document: read it as ok. Read status before faults.

fields.meaning: ok for every analysis from 1.4.0. A document written before ADR-0012 can carry a refusal: different_movement, not_enough_visible or moving_part_out_of_frame.
fields.notes: A refusal has faults [] and score null. It is not a take with no faults: leave it out of fault counts.

fields.meaning: Why the grade is capped at F: a list of {code, text}. Codes: low_match, moving_part_out_of_frame, not_enough_visible, no_usable_measures, and no_person (written only by Part 7's own analysis).
fields.present_when: The take earned a warning.
fields.notes: The take is still analysed on the measures the camera sees. Any warning caps score.value at 59. On a low match every fault has confidence low and every tempo is null. no_person arrived in 1.9.0. Keep these takes apart from takes with no warning, or count them separately.

fields.meaning: The reason for one warning.
fields.present_when: The take earned a warning.
fields.notes: A new code can appear in a later minor version. Part 5 never writes no_person.

fields.meaning: How closely the take matches the trainer's movement: quality, residual, timing_corr and the limits they were judged against.
fields.present_when: The take earned a warning. Absent otherwise, and in Part 7's no_person document, where nothing was compared.
fields.notes: residual and timing_corr are null when they were not measured.

fields.meaning: ok or low. Low exactly when the movement guard would have refused the take.
fields.present_when: The take earned a warning.
fields.notes: Low means every fault has confidence low and every tempo is null.

fields.meaning: How well the camera saw the follower's take (simon.quality.v1): level, reasons, signals and score_cap.
fields.present_when: Every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0. Absent means not assessed: a document written before 1.13.0, or by another producer. Detect it by presence.
fields.notes: Reported only. score.value, score.grade, score.fault_cap, score.uncapped, score.capped_by and warnings are what they are without it, and it never adds a warnings entry. Part 7 applies score_cap. A take with no quality was not assessed; do not read it as ok. Leave a degraded or major take out of a pattern across takes, or count it apart: a poorly seen take says little about the person's movement.

fields.meaning: Which formula and meaning the block has: simon.quality.v1.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A change of meaning would be a new version. Compare levels only between takes that carry the same version.

fields.meaning: ok, degraded or major: the worst reason, ok when there is none.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: The order runs ok, degraded, major, best to worst. major means score_cap is 59. The limits are in part5/quality.json and are not in rules.json. Part 5 sets no cap, grade or gate from the level.

fields.meaning: The reasons for the level, in a fixed order; empty for ok.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: At most one reason for each signal, at the higher limit it reached, and the three warning reasons first.

fields.meaning: One reason: {code, words, value, threshold} and, where one joint is the cause, joint.
fields.present_when: quality.reasons is not empty (level is degraded or major).
fields.notes: Show words as it is. Group by code, never by words.

fields.meaning: Why: not_enough_visible, moving_part_out_of_frame, no_usable_measures, joints_unseen, joints_missing, frames_missing, measures_hidden, position_jitter or, from 1.14.0, heading_offset (TICKET-086).
fields.present_when: quality.reasons is not empty (level is degraded or major).
fields.notes: A closed list. The first three repeat a warning the take carries (always major, value and threshold null). low_match is never a reason. A later minor version may add a code: tolerate one you do not know.

fields.meaning: One plain sentence made from the measured numbers.
fields.present_when: quality.reasons is not empty (level is degraded or major).
fields.notes: It names no cause (light, a hand over the lens): Part 5 has no reading for one. It is template text that may be revised, so do not group by it.

fields.meaning: The reading of the signal behind the reason, in that signal's unit.
fields.present_when: quality.reasons is not empty (level is degraded or major).
fields.notes: A share from 0 to 1 for the four share signals, millimetres per frame for position_jitter. null for a warning reason.

fields.meaning: The limit the reading reached, in the same unit as value.
fields.present_when: quality.reasons is not empty (level is degraded or major).
fields.notes: The degraded or the major limit of part5/quality.json (the higher one reached). null for a warning reason.

fields.meaning: The joint with the largest reading, as a canonical joint name.
fields.present_when: A joints_unseen, joints_missing or position_jitter reason names a joint.
fields.notes: Only on joints_unseen, joints_missing and position_jitter, and only when a joint is the largest. The performer's own left and right, like faults[].joint.

fields.meaning: The five raw readings behind the level.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings.

fields.meaning: Share of the readings, among the joints the example itself sees, at Part 2's 0.3 unseen mark, counted as ADR-0011 counts it (a joint is unseen when its left or right counterpart is at 0.3 too).
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings. null when the follower file carries no conf or the example sees no joint. The example's joints are those it sees in at least half of its frames (its own conf or --expected-visibility); an example with no conf counts every joint, so a waist-up follower against a waist-up trainer that carries no conf still reads its legs as unseen.

fields.meaning: Share of the joint readings that are null or have conf below 0.3.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings.

fields.meaning: Share of the frames flagged interpolated or with at most half of the 17 joints usable.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings.

fields.meaning: Share of the full-body measures the example shows (all 22 when its visibility is unknown) that the follower's own conf makes unusable under ADR-0011.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings. null when the follower file carries no conf or the example shows no full-body measure. It reads the follower's own conf over the measures the example shows (from Part 5 1.14.2, TICKET-107; before that over all 22), not the pair's: diagnostics.visibility.excluded is the pair's.

fields.meaning: Frame-to-frame jitter of the joint positions in millimetres per frame: feet.jitter of the step series of each joint and axis, the axes joined as a norm, the median over the joints.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: A signal is a raw reading of the follower's file, read before smoothing. null means it could not be made, never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings. It depends on the file's frame rate (per frame, not per second), so compare it between takes of one frame rate.

fields.meaning: The heading left between the example and the follower after Part 3's facing step: the median over the aligned frame pairs of the angle, 0 to 180 degrees, between the two bodies' headings in the horizontal plane (the hip and shoulder lines, left minus right).
fields.present_when: quality is present in a document from 1.14.0 (every document Part 5 writes); a 1.13.0 quality block has no such key.
fields.notes: Read after alignment, unlike the other signals, which read the follower's file alone. null means it could not be made (the take could not be aligned, or no aligned pair had a hip or shoulder line), never 0 (0.0 is a measured zero). It is reported only: it does not change score.value, score.grade, the faults or the warnings. Past 5 degrees the block adds the reason heading_offset, degraded only (the heading alone never makes a take major, so it never brings the cap of 59; TICKET-086, Part 7's choice): the take was filmed from another angle than the example, and TICKET-082 measured that this moves the score, so treat such a score as rough and leave it out of a comparison across takes.

fields.meaning: 59 when level is major, else null.
fields.present_when: quality is present (every document Part 5 writes from 1.13.0).
fields.notes: Reported only. 59 is score.WARNING_CAP, the cap a warning puts on score.value. Part 5 does not apply it: a major take can carry a score.value above 59, and Part 7 applies the cap.

fields.meaning: One reported fault: a measure, on a side, in one direction, that crossed its threshold, lasted long enough to count and was not explained by another kept fault.
fields.notes: The list is sorted by |magnitude_deg|, largest first, not by time. An empty list is a correct take, a take nothing could be measured on, or an old refusal: read warnings and status before treating it as no faults. Identify a fault across takes by measure, side and direction.

fields.meaning: What differed, side-less (upper_arm_out, knee_flexion, trunk_lean_forward). See measures for what more and less mean for each.
fields.notes: foot_rotation and ankle_inversion arrived in 1.6.0 and only appear when a feet file was given for the pair. Tolerate a measure you do not know. A score version does not rename a measure.

fields.meaning: angle for a joint angle (elbow_flexion, knee_flexion), direction for the direction of a segment (every other measure).
fields.notes: Both kinds are in degrees.

fields.meaning: Where it differed: a sided joint (left_elbow), the side-stripped joint for side both (elbow), or spine, shoulders or neck for a centre measure.
fields.notes: left_ankle and right_ankle for the foot measures, ankle for both.

fields.meaning: The canonical joints to highlight: the one joint, or the left and the right for side both.
fields.notes: A 1.0 document has none. Then map joint as CONTRACT.md duty 3 says.

fields.meaning: The body part: arms, legs, torso, head or feet.
fields.notes: feet arrived in 1.6.0 with the two foot measures.

fields.meaning: Which side of the performer's body: left, right, both or center.
fields.notes: The performer's own left and right, not the image's. both is the two sides merged; center has no side. See side_convention.

fields.meaning: more or less than the example: the sign of follower minus example.
fields.notes: more is a positive magnitude_deg and less a negative one. Neither is worse: both are departures. What more means depends on the measure; see measures.

fields.meaning: The size of the fault: follower minus example, signed, the median over the counted runs of the smoothed per-frame difference, to 0.1 degree. For side both, the mean of the two sides.
fields.notes: Degrees for every measure, not a ratio and not scaled to body size or clip length. To compare two measures divide by threshold_deg. The sign equals direction. A score version does not change it. trunk_lean_side before 2026-10-31 is not comparable when the trunk hinged forward past about 90 degrees (detection_changes_without_a_version).

fields.meaning: The largest difference in the counted runs, with its sign.
fields.notes: Same sign as magnitude_deg. For side both, the larger of the two sides.

fields.meaning: The size the difference had to pass to count, for this measure under this profile.
fields.notes: Read it from the fault; do not assume one value per measure. Thresholds come from part5/rules.json and differ by measure and by profile, and the rules were recalibrated by held-out attempts (docs/thresholds.md). |magnitude_deg| / threshold_deg is the ratio the score charges on.

fields.meaning: The unit of the sizes of this fault. Always degrees.
fields.notes: The schema allows only the value degrees.

fields.meaning: Where in the expected movement the fault's reported run starts and ends, as a fraction.
fields.notes: 0 is the start of the expected movement and 1 its end. For a take compared repetition by repetition the contract does not say which part of the expected clip the fraction is taken over, so use it for a take compared as a whole. expected_frames and follower_frames are clip-specific and left out of this list.

fields.meaning: The share of the counted frames in which both clips had the measure.
fields.notes: A lower value means more of the evidence was masked.

fields.meaning: How far past its threshold the fault was, times coverage, from 0 to 1. On a low match, the string low instead.
fields.notes: Not a probability, and not a severity: it says how sure the detection is, not how bad the fault is. The string low arrived in 1.4.0. Do not average low with numbers; set low faults apart.

fields.meaning: The moment to seek to: follower_t_s[0] rounded half up to 0.1 s, on the follower file's own clock.
fields.notes: Absent means the fault is untimed (a document before 1.2.0). For a take compared repetition by repetition it is the time in the first repetition the fault was found in; the other repetitions are in reps.

fields.meaning: [start, end] in seconds on the follower file's own clock, at follower_frames[0] and [1].
fields.notes: Absent as for at_s. The end minus the start is how long the reported run lasted; a fault held in several stretches has more runs than this span.

fields.meaning: Every counted run of the fault, as [start, end] frames of the expected clip.
fields.notes: Frames of the example, not seconds, so counts compare across takes of one example but frame numbers do not compare across examples. The number of runs says in how many separate stretches the fault was held.

fields.meaning: The same runs as frames of the follower file as written, in the same order as runs.
fields.notes: Frames of the follower file, which may have a different frame rate from the example. Use follower_t_s for time.

fields.meaning: The follower repetitions (0-based, in order) the fault was found in.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition (score.basis is reps).
fields.notes: Since attempt 4 (ADR-0017) every take of an example with two or more repetitions is compared this way. at_s, follower_t_s and follower_runs are those of the first repetition listed. The number of follower repetitions is the length of diagnostics.guard.reps. From 1.12.0 faults[].rep_sizes gives the fault's size in each of these repetitions.

fields.meaning: The fault's size in each repetition that found it: a list of {rep, magnitude_deg, side, body_part}, one entry for each repetition in faults[].reps, in the same order.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition (score.basis is reps).
fields.notes: It lets a report say which repetition was worst, and compare the same repetition across sessions. The fault's own magnitude_deg is the median of the entries on its side (every entry for a fault on both). A repetition the guard refused has no entry. No fault, score or insight reads it. A document written before 1.12.0 does not have it.

fields.meaning: The follower repetition the entry is for, counted from 0.
fields.present_when: The fault has rep_sizes.
fields.notes: The same index as faults[].reps and score.per_rep[].rep, so the three join on it.

fields.meaning: The fault's size in that repetition, in degrees: the follower's value minus the example's.
fields.present_when: The fault has rep_sizes.
fields.notes: Signed like faults[].magnitude_deg: more is positive and less is negative. A repetition that found both sides gives the mean of the two. Divide by faults[].threshold_deg to compare faults of different measures.

fields.meaning: The side that repetition found the fault on: left, right, both or center.
fields.present_when: The fault has rep_sizes.
fields.notes: The performer's own side. It can differ from faults[].side: a fault reported on one side counts a repetition that found both sides (side both), and a fault reported on both counts a repetition that found one side.

fields.meaning: The body part of that repetition's occurrence: arms, legs, torso, head or feet.
fields.present_when: The fault has rep_sizes.
fields.notes: The same body part as faults[].body_part for the same measure.

fields.meaning: Which way the part is off, in the performer's own frame: left, right, or null when no direction applies.
fields.notes: Worked out from measure, direction and side. It is the performer's left and right, like side.

fields.meaning: On a foot_out fault with side left or right: the median metres the ankle is further out than the example's, to 0.01 m.
fields.present_when: The fault is foot_out on one side.
fields.notes: The only length in a fault. Positive is further out than the example. Every other size is in degrees.

fields.meaning: The plain-words line, a lowercase fragment: "right elbow bent more than the example".
fields.notes: Template text in English that carries a size word chosen from |magnitude_deg| / threshold_deg (slightly under 1.5, much from 3, otherwise none), so the same fault reads differently at different sizes. The wording has been revised over time. Display only: never group or compare by it.

fields.meaning: The timed words plus " at <at_s> s": "right foot too far right at 1.9 s".
fields.notes: Absent means show text. It carries the same size word as text and the same caution: display only.

fields.meaning: The line a phrasing backend wrote for this fault. For the template it equals text_timed.
fields.notes: May be live model text in the follower's language when live mode is on (phrasing.faults[].text equals it from 1.9.0). It never changes a measure, a score or a cue. Display only.

fields.meaning: What to do, an imperative of at most 6 words: "Bend your knees more".
fields.notes: Template text from measure, direction and side only, so the same fault always gets the same cue within one vocabulary; a phrasing backend never rewrites it. The vocabulary grew with the foot measures in 1.6.0. Absent means a document older than 1.5.0. Group by measure, side and direction, not by cue.

fields.meaning: range when the fix is how far a joint bends or a limb lifts; position when it is where a body part is placed or aligned.
fields.notes: tempo is a third kind that only an insight carries.

fields.meaning: The take's score block: version, value, grade, components, params_sha256 and, when present, basis, timeline, tempo, per_rep, fault_cap, uncapped and capped_by.
fields.notes: Never null from 1.4.0. Null in a refusal of 1.3.0 or earlier, and absent when the producer does not score. Part 7's no_person document carries only version, value and grade.

fields.meaning: Which score made the value: simon.score.v1, simon.score.v2 or simon.score.v3.
fields.notes: Compare score.value only within one version. v2 arrived in 1.10.0 and v3 in 1.11.0 as values of the same field. See score_versions. Do not infer it from schema_version.

fields.meaning: The take's score, 0 to 100: the mean of its compared windows, then capped.
fields.notes: An integer. Compare only within one score.version and one profile. A take with a warning is capped at 59. Under v2 and v3 a take that reports a fault is capped at score.fault_cap. A 0 with a warning (no_usable_measures, or Part 7's no_person) means nothing could be measured, not the worst possible take. score.uncapped.value is the value before the caps when one lowered it.

fields.meaning: The letter for value: A 90 and above, B 80 to 89, C 70 to 79, D 60 to 69, F below 60.
fields.notes: The bands are the same in v1, v2 and v3. The same letter in two profiles or two score versions is not the same standard.

fields.meaning: The SHA-256 of the score block of part5/rules.json that produced the score.
fields.notes: A fingerprint of the scoring parameters. It covers the whole block, the frozen v1 and v2 blocks included, and is the same in every profile. Equal hashes mean the same parameters. It says nothing about detection. Absent in Part 7's no_person document.

fields.meaning: The points taken off the take: faults, similarity and, under the dance profile, tempo.
fields.notes: Means over the compared windows, before any cap, so they add up to 100 minus the value only when no cap lowered it. components.tempo arrived in 1.7.0 and only under dance.

fields.meaning: What the timeline's windows are: windows (about 5 s slices of a take compared as a whole) or reps (one window per repetition).
fields.notes: ADR-0013. With basis windows, a window index does not mean the same stretch of movement in two takes: the slices are equal cuts of each take's own span. since is the version that made it always written: a 1.2.0, 1.3.0 or 1.4.0 document (by content) written after 05312b7 and before d3250dc can already hold it (score_changes_without_a_version).

fields.meaning: The ceiling in force on the value for a take that reports a fault.
fields.present_when: The take's faults list is not empty and score.version is simon.score.v2 or simon.score.v3.
fields.notes: v2: 89 for any fault. v3 (1.11.0): 89 for one fault and 79 for two or more. Written whether or not it lowered the value. Read it, never assume 89. It is not a warning, and capped_by never names it.

fields.meaning: {value, grade} before the caps, so a reader can say what a cap cost.
fields.present_when: A cap lowered the value.
fields.notes: In 1.9.0 it was the value before the warning cap only. From 1.10.0 it is the value before every cap, the fault cap and the warning cap, and with both it is the value before the first. For the pre-cap score of any take read uncapped.value when present, else value.

fields.meaning: The warning codes behind the cap at 59.
fields.present_when: The take has warnings.
fields.notes: Written whether or not the cap lowered the value, and never the fault cap. Use score.uncapped to tell whether it did.

fields.meaning: The value and grade of each accepted repetition; the take's value is their mean, before any cap.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition.
fields.notes: Only repetitions that passed the guard are listed, so its length can be shorter than the number of follower repetitions in diagnostics.guard.reps. From 1.12.0 each entry also has rep and tempo_ratio.

fields.meaning: One repetition's score, 0 to 100.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition.
fields.notes: Never capped: the fault cap and the warning cap are applied once, to the mean, so a repetition can score above score.value. Same score.version as the take.

fields.meaning: The follower repetition the entry is for, counted from 0.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition.
fields.notes: Only the accepted repetitions are listed, so the position in the list is not the repetition: join on rep. It is also the position of the repetition's window in score.timeline, and the rep of faults[].reps and faults[].rep_sizes[].rep. A document before 1.12.0 has no rep on its entries.

fields.meaning: That repetition's pace: follower seconds per example second.
fields.present_when: The take was compared repetition by repetition.
fields.notes: Equal to the tempo.ratio of score.timeline[rep], to 0.01. Null where the repetition could not be timed (the example's repetition spans under 1 s) and for every repetition of a take with match.quality low: null means not measured, never on time (absent_means.tempo). On time is a ratio from 0.85 to 1.15. Under the rehab profile a ratio above 1.15 is not held against the take.

fields.meaning: The take's tempo: {ratio, cue}, for the whole take or the median of its repetitions.
fields.notes: Not scored, except under the dance profile, which charges it into components.tempo. See absent_means.tempo.

fields.meaning: Follower seconds per example second for the same stretch of movement, to 0.01. Below 1 the follower was faster, above 1 slower.
fields.notes: Null means not measured, never on time (TICKET-063): a low match, or an example stretch under 1 s. A document written before TICKET-063 can carry a number for a low match take.

fields.meaning: Slow down to match the trainer below 0.85, Speed up to match the trainer above 1.15 (Slower is fine under rehab), otherwise null.
fields.notes: Null with a ratio means on pace; null with a null ratio means not measured. Under the rehab profile a ratio above 1.15 reads Slower is fine (ADR-0016), a reassurance and not a fault. The schema's enum for this field lists null, the two default cues and Slower is fine (TICKET-073 added the rehab cue, which the producer has written since 1.7.0 and the enum had omitted; no schema_version change), so a document validates under any profile and the cue can be read as one of those four values.

fields.meaning: The take window by window: the score block's evidence for the value.
fields.notes: ADR-0013. The take's value is the mean of the compared windows, then capped. Absent on the zero score of a take that could not be aligned. since is the version that made it always written: a 1.2.0, 1.3.0 or 1.4.0 document (by content) written after 05312b7 and before d3250dc can already hold it (score_changes_without_a_version).

fields.meaning: [start, end] of the window in seconds on the follower file's own clock, to 0.001 s.
fields.notes: The end of the last window is the end of the compared span, which is the follower's duration only when the whole clip was compared (CONTRACT.md duty 10).

fields.meaning: Whether anything in the window could be scored.
fields.notes: false means the window has no value, no misses and no tempo, and does not count toward the mean.

fields.meaning: The window's score, 0 to 100: 100 minus its misses' points and its similarity term.
fields.present_when: The window was compared.
fields.notes: Never capped; the caps apply to the take's value.

fields.meaning: The window's tempo: {ratio, cue}, read like score.tempo.
fields.present_when: The window was compared.
fields.notes: Null ratio and cue when the window's example side spans under 1 s, and for every window of a low match take (TICKET-063). Under dance the window is charged for it in components.tempo.

fields.meaning: One miss: a fault that cost the window points. The list is how the number is justified.
fields.present_when: The window was compared and a fault covered it.
fields.notes: A fault found across many repetitions appears as a miss in each window it covers, with its own points. Carries text, measure, side, joint, t_s, at_s, points, cue, cue_kind and direction.

fields.meaning: The score points the miss cost its window, to 0.1.
fields.present_when: The window was compared and a fault covered it.
fields.notes: On the window's scale, before the caps and before the mean. Its size depends on score.version (v2 and v3 weight it by how much the trainer moves the measure), so compare within one version.

fields.meaning: The measure of the fault the miss came from.
fields.present_when: The window was compared and a fault covered it.
fields.notes: The same vocabulary as faults[].measure.

fields.meaning: The side of the fault the miss came from: left, right, both or center.
fields.present_when: The window was compared and a fault covered it.
fields.notes: The performer's own side, as in faults[].side. The schema allows null.

fields.meaning: The fault's direction, more or less than the example.
fields.present_when: The window was compared and a fault covered it.
fields.notes: Same meaning as faults[].direction.

fields.meaning: The DDR style credit display beside the score (simon.credit.v1): {percent, grade, points, max_points} at the level named by tolerance, the same for each of levels easy, normal and hard, and per_window, one entry for each compared window of score.timeline.
fields.notes: Null when nothing was compared. Additive: score.value, score.grade and the caps do not read it, and the warning cap of 59 does not apply to it, so a take with warnings can show a high credit percent; read warnings first. percent is credit earned over credit possible; points count 100 per measure per second on the example's clock, so they grow with the example's length and the measures seen, not with how long the follower took: compare percent across takes, and points only between takes of one example, and only within one credit version and one profile.

fields.meaning: Credit earned over credit possible at the level named by score.credit.tolerance (normal), 0 to 100, to 0.1.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: 100 * points / max_points, so each window weighs by its seconds and the measures counted in it. Reported only: it sets no grade, cap or gate, and score.value does not read it. The one credit number to compare across takes, within one profile. From Part 5 1.14.2 (TICKET-108) the take's last second earns full credit, in each measure the example moves away in, when the follower holds still there.

fields.meaning: Credit earned at the level named by score.credit.tolerance: 100 points per measure per second held within half a threshold.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: Grows with the example's length and the measures seen, not with how long the follower took, so compare it only with max_points of the same take, and between takes only when they follow one example.

fields.meaning: The points the example's length and the measures counted could earn: 100 per measure per second on the example's clock.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: Read with points; it is not a target.

fields.meaning: {easy, normal, hard}, each {percent, points, max_points}: easy scales the thresholds by 1.5 and the points by 0.75, normal by 1.0 and 1.0, hard by 0.7 and 1.5.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: The top-level percent, points and max_points are the normal level's. A level's percent compares only with the same level.

fields.meaning: One {t_s, percent, points, max_points} for each compared window of score.timeline, the same t_s, in the same order, at the normal level.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: percent is null in a window where no measure was seen in half its frames. A window that was not compared has no entry.

fields.meaning: Which credit formula made the block: simon.credit.v1.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: Compare score.credit.percent only between takes that carry the same version, the same tolerance and the same profile.

fields.meaning: The letter for score.credit.percent on the credit's own scale, score.credit.grades: S 95 and above, A 85 to 94.9, B 75 to 84.9, C 65 to 74.9, D 55 to 64.9, E 45 to 54.9, F below 45 (F's mark is 30, and under 30 is still F).
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: Informational. Not the score's grade: score.grade is the letter for score.value under the score's bands (A to F), and the two can differ, for a take capped to F can show a credit grade of B; S and E are credit letters only. Reported only, it sets no cap and no gate, and it ignores warnings and caps. The scale is the team's game scale (ADR-0020).

fields.meaning: The level that the top-level percent, points and max_points are shown at: easy, normal or hard.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: normal in every simon.credit.v1 document. The three levels are all under score.credit.levels.

fields.meaning: [z / tolerance at most, credit] from the tightest band, as [[0.5, 1.0], [1.0, 0.6], [2.0, 0.2]]; beyond the last band the credit is 0.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: The credit a measure earns on a frame, by how far the follower is from the example in that measure's detection thresholds. A constant of the credit version, listed so a reader can show the rule.

fields.meaning: The credit's letter grades, [percent at least, letter] from the highest, as [[95, "S"], [85, "A"], [75, "B"], [65, "C"], [55, "D"], [45, "E"], [30, "F"]]: score.credit.grade is the first letter score.credit.percent reaches, and a percent under the last is still F.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: The team's game scale for the credit (ADR-0020), not the score's bands: score.value and score.grade do not use it. A constant of the credit version, listed so a reader can draw the marks.

fields.meaning: How many points one measure earns for one second held at full credit: 100.
fields.present_when: score.credit is not null (the take was compared).
fields.notes: A constant of the credit version. points and max_points count it per measure per second, times the level's multiplier.

fields.meaning: One thing to work on first: {cue, why, kind, at_s, window, points}.
fields.notes: At most 5, ranked by the points they cost the score, with a tempo item last when the tempo has an action cue. It is a short list, so a fault missing from it is not a fault that did not happen: count faults from faults[] or the misses. Under rehab the reassurance Slower is fine is not an item.

fields.meaning: position, range or tempo.
fields.present_when: The document has an insight.
fields.notes: The first two are the cue_kind of the fault behind the insight; tempo is the pace item.

fields.meaning: What the cue cost the score: its share, summed over the compared windows and divided by their number.
fields.present_when: The document has an insight.
fields.notes: Null for a tempo item outside the dance profile (under dance it equals score.components.tempo, ADR-0016) and for a take without a timeline.

fields.meaning: false while no native reader has checked the language of the take's lines, cues and reasons (phrasing.lang): the text is a model's and has not been reviewed by a native reader.
fields.present_when: phrasing.lang is a listed language other than en (a request in en, or in a tag Part 5 does not list, has no native_review).
fields.notes: false for every language today (none has been signed off). Never a measure of the movement: a report across takes does not rank on it; a viewer shows it as a note. true would mean a person who reads the language has checked the text.

fields.meaning: One cue or reason of the document written in the follower's language: {path, text, lang, backend, model, fallback_reason}, in document order.
fields.present_when: phrasing.lang is a listed language other than en. [] when the document has no cue or reason.
fields.notes: Additive: the English fields it translates (faults[].cue, the misses' and tempo cues, insights[].cue and insights[].why) do not change, so compare takes on those, not on text. An entry whose backend is template kept the field's English text.

fields.meaning: The field the entry is about: faults[0].cue, score.timeline[2].misses[0].cue, score.timeline[2].tempo.cue, score.tempo.cue, insights[1].cue or insights[1].why.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: An index is a position in this document's own list; it is not stable across takes.

fields.meaning: The cue or reason to show, in phrasing.cues[].lang.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: Free text from a model, or the English template text when it fell back. Do not group takes by it; group by the English cue.

fields.meaning: The language of phrasing.cues[].text: the requested language, or en for an entry that kept the English text.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: A BCP 47 primary subtag from the listed languages (part5/phrasing/lang.py).

fields.meaning: Who wrote phrasing.cues[].text: muse-spark or local-llm, or template for an entry that kept the English text.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: The provenance of the text: a template is never a translation. The value set may grow.

fields.meaning: The model that wrote phrasing.cues[].text, null when the template kept the English text.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: For example meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026.

fields.meaning: Why phrasing.cues[].text is the English text: null when the model's text is shown, else a short reason such as muse-spark: translation adds a number, rate limited or no key.
fields.present_when: The entry exists.
fields.notes: Never a key or the model's text.

fields.meaning: The candidate faults detection considered and dropped: {total, omitted, items}.
fields.notes: For people debugging a take; not shown to the follower, and the Part 5 docs call diagnostics pipeline internals. It changes no fault, score or insight. See absent_means.near_misses.

fields.meaning: How many candidates were considered and dropped.
fields.notes: 0 means nothing came past a threshold. A take compared repetition by repetition counts a candidate once, at the take level.

fields.meaning: One dropped candidate, sized like a fault: measure, side, joint, body_part, direction, magnitude_deg, peak_deg, threshold_deg, frames_over, counted_frames, needed_frames and a reason, and from 1.12.0 margin_deg.
fields.present_when: A candidate was dropped. At most 10 are listed, largest first.
fields.notes: magnitude_deg is in degrees and signed like a fault's. A near miss is not a fault and not a half fault.

fields.meaning: left, right or center. Never both.
fields.present_when: A candidate was dropped.
fields.notes: Sides are merged for reported faults only, so match a near miss to a both fault by measure and direction on either side.

fields.meaning: Why it was dropped: persistence, explained_by, reps or fitness.
fields.present_when: A candidate was dropped.
fields.notes: persistence: too few counted frames. explained_by: a kept fault explains it. reps and fitness appear only for a take compared repetition by repetition.

fields.meaning: How far the candidate's size was past its threshold, in degrees: abs(magnitude_deg) minus threshold_deg, to 0.1 degree.
fields.present_when: A candidate was dropped.
fields.notes: Positive: past the threshold by that many degrees before the candidate was dropped, whatever the reason (persistence, explained_by, reps or fitness). 0: on the threshold. Negative: short of it. Detection lists only candidates with a frame past the threshold, so every value written today is 0 or more; tolerate a negative one. It is the margin of the size, not of the peak: for the peak read abs(peak_deg) minus threshold_deg. A document before 1.12.0 does not have it.

fields.meaning: The sided measures left out of the comparison because the camera did not see them (for example left_knee_flexion).
fields.present_when: The take was compared on fewer measures than the full body (ADR-0011).
fields.notes: A measure listed here was not measured, so its absence from faults[] is not evidence of a good take. diagnostics.visibility is absent when every measure was usable.

fields.meaning: The foot measures (left_foot_rotation, right_ankle_inversion and so on) the pair was compared on.
fields.present_when: A feet file was given for either clip.
fields.notes: A foot fault can only exist for a measure listed here. Without diagnostics.feet no foot measure was compared.

fields.meaning: Why no foot measure was compared, in plain words; null when any was.
fields.present_when: A feet file was given for either clip.
fields.notes: Examples: no file, a file with no foot points, too few frames seen, nothing steady enough to read.

not_listed.why: Frames of the example. They compare across takes of one example but not across examples; use phase or follower_t_s.
Frames of the follower file as written, which can have another frame rate. Use follower_t_s.
Records who wrote faults[].coaching. It changes no measure, cue or score.
A model's view of the take, labelled model_opinion. The score, faults and insights never read it.

Pipeline internals for debugging, not shown to the follower. Only the near misses, the visibility exclusions and the feet block are listed because they tell a measure that was not measured from one that was fine.
The part that produced the document. Absent means part5, and Part 5 never writes it.
